summary: Philipp André Maas is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (by 2004) under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler, and has held posts at Bonn, the University of Vienna, and the University of Leipzig.

Philippe Stern (1895–1979) was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He held positions at the Guimet Museum (1927–1965), the Musée de la parole et du geste (c. 1928–1937), and the École du Louvre (1929–1965).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) was a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, Collège de France (1857, 1870–1894), and University of Paris (c. 1862–1894).
Phillip Bloom is a scholar of archaeology and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He has served as Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat (c. 1996), Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (c. 1997–2018), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (c. 2007).

Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, and also studied under Phrathepyanmahamuni.
Phrapongsak K. is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 2015, he held research positions at Ryukoku University and the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and has held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff (born 1947) works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University (c. 1973) and served as Professor at McMaster University (c. 1976–2004) before becoming Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (2004).
Pierre Arènes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under André Bareau and held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2003–2004).

Pierre Bourdieu (1930–2002) was a philosopher and sociologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at Lille University of Science and Technology (c. 1961–1964), the EHESS (1975), and the Collège de France (1981–2001).
Pierre Chantraine (1899–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes. He held a post at the University of Paris from circa 1938 to 1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the EFEO and French Institute of Pondicherry (1963–1967), the École Pratique des Hautes Études as Chair of Sanskrit (1967–2004), and was President of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (2010).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University in 1991, where he was also attested as a Research-Fellow in 1996.
Pieter Hendrik Pott (1918–1989) worked in Tibetology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as curator at Museum Volkenkunde (c. 1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

Pietro Merlo (1850–1888) studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin (1867). He taught at the University of Pavia from 1877, becoming extraordinary professor in 1880 and full professor of comparative linguistics in 1885.
